correctness.rationale: For a finite theory, finitely many raw nouns induce finitely many Boolean atoms with nonnegative integer multiplicities. Every Boolean noun cardinality is a 0/1 linear form in those multiplicities, and each of the four syllogistic sentence types translates exactly to a linear equality or inequality. Existential projection gives a Presburger definition of total size. Uniform replication proves dilation closure independently. The displayed arbitrary-k theory forces a disjoint equal-block partition and realizes exactly the positive multiples of k.

value.rationale: The primary source shows that noun-level union immediately escapes its complete base-language spectrum classification, making the expressive frontier a motivated open structural question. The accepted theorem supplies a global arithmetic ceiling for every finite theory—effective ultimate periodicity—while also showing exact divisibility by every modulus. This rules out genuinely nonperiodic spectra such as primes and powers of two and sharply locates the noun-Boolean extension between the source's simple tail spectra and unrestricted finite-spectrum behavior.
